# Read Deep, Write Shallow: How Looped Language Models Should Spend Their Depth

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models run one block of layers several times per token and use the same number of
> loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to write the answer (decode). This work separates the two with a small
> depth-split connector (LoRA + per-loop RoPE-commuting KV maps on a frozen model) and measures what each depth buys on
> Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B, Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, Nanbeige4.2-3B and SenseNova-Loop-9B.

Main claims (quotable, with numbers):
- In looped language models, depth spent reading the prompt buys understanding, while depth spent writing the answer buys
  multi-step derivation. Ouro-2.6B, one writing loop, read 4 vs read 1 loops: MMLU +15.2, RULER-16K +8.6 (same under a
  second training seed).
- Reading deeper rescues a collapsed shallow writer without training: SenseNova-Loop-9B's one-loop writer, given a
  two-loop prompt state, cuts unanswered GSM8K problems from 97% to 44% and lifts RULER-4K from 21.6 to 83.5.
- Writing shallow is where time is saved: a 2-loop writer comes within one point of the 4-loop Ouro-2.6B-Thinking on GSM8K
  at 0.55x its time per answer; a 1-loop writer on SenseNova-Loop-9B matches the 2-loop model at 0.59x.
- A per-frequency complex scale commutes with RoPE, so one stored prompt KV cache serves every loop exactly; storing the
  answer once too gives 2.17x the long-answer decode throughput of native 4/4.
- Shallow KV keeps what was said, deep KV keeps what comes next: in the value cache, the previous token becomes less and
  the next token more linearly decodable from loop 1 to 4 (57.7 -> 45.5%, 26.0 -> 36.1%); reading deep costs 4-shot MATH
  (-9.8) but helps zero-shot MATH (+7.0).

Limitations stated by the author: short-context verbatim retrieval prefers shallow KV; at three or more writing loops a
single deep prompt bank trails the native model on retrieval; deeper prefill raises time to first token; 1.4B models
collapse at read 4 / write 1 on few-shot CoT BBH; a shared answer bank costs 2.6 GSM8K points at write 4; gains against
native models include adaptation.

Related: Ouro (2510.25741), Continuous Depth Batching (2608.09444), OverFill (2508.08446), Fixed Points II (2610.06833),
Looped Latent Attention (2607.15456), BeNice! (2610.31633), Elastic Latent Recurrence (2610.12582), Parallel Loop
Transformer (2510.24824), Shared Memory in Looped Transformers (2610.02383), Decode-Branch Transformers (2608.12385).
